note.after_visit_summary: You came in feeling very tired for about six weeks and feeling dizzy when you first stand up. You had no chest pain, shortness of breath, fever, or weight loss. Your heart rate was slow at 52, and your blood pressure dropped when you stood up. The doctor thinks your tiredness comes mostly from your medicines: metoprolol can slow your heart too much, and Tylenol PM makes many older adults drowsy all day. Please stop taking Tylenol PM. For night aches, you may use acetaminophen 500 mg. Take metoprolol 25 mg twice a day instead of 50 mg. Keep taking amlodipine, atorvastatin, and baby aspirin the same. Get up slowly and sit on the edge of your bed before standing. For sleep, go to bed at the same time, avoid long afternoon naps, and get morning light. Vitamin D will become a chewable 1000 units once a day. You are getting blood tests today. Call us or go to the emergency room if you faint, get chest pain, or notice a slower pulse. We will see you in 2 weeks to review your test results.
